facts.material: finely knit 100% cotton fabric (cotton assumed predominant in all pieces)
facts.function: infant sleep and play wear with coordinating bib
facts.form: retail set of a bodysuit, a stretchsuit (one-piece sleeper) and a bib

gri_path: GRI 1: heading 6111 covers babies' garments and clothing accessories, knitted; chapter 61 note 6(b) gives 6111 priority over other chapter 61 headings

Additional U.S. Note 1 to chapter 61 (as quoted in N356719): 'sets' are two or more different garments of 6111 imported together, of corresponding sizes, intended to be worn together by the same person; bodysuit, stretchsuit and bib are marketed as one outfit
GRI 6: 6111.20 of cotton; 6111.20.10-.50 exclude goods imported as parts of sets, so 6111.20.60; statistical suffix .20 Sets (239)

rejected_alternatives.reason: line for bodysuits/washsuits when entered individually; applies if the pieces do not meet the Additional U.S. Note 1 set definition (then bodysuit and stretchsuit each here, bib in 6111.20.60.70)
bib alone as an accessory; used only if the items are not a set
chapter 61 note 6(b) gives heading 6111 priority for babies' garments

missing_facts: Are the bodysuit, stretchsuit and bib of corresponding sizes and intended to be worn together at the same time (Additional U.S. Note 1 set test)? If not, the bodysuit (first-named) goes to 6111.20.60.10.
classification.rationale: Infant garments of knitted cotton fall in heading 6111 under GRI 1 and chapter 61 note 6. The item is sold as a coordinated set of different babies' garments; under Additional U.S. Note 1 to chapter 61 (quoted in NY N356719, in force) such sets fall outside the 'except parts of sets' lines and go to 6111.20.60, statistical line Sets (.20). If CBP found the pieces are not worn together, each would be classified separately as in N014992 (bodysuit at 6111.20.6010, bib at 6111.20.6070).
